analysis.session_summary: The tape was a two-speed session: AUD strength dominated early after Australia's July CPI beat (AUD +0.445% vs majors), while USD strength took over into the NY morning despite an inline core PCE print (USD +0.227%). The USD bid was broad through USD/CHF, USD/CAD and USD/JPY, and EUR/USD closed at the lower end of a 37.4-pip range. Gold (-1.115%) and BTC (-1.473%) sagged even as VIX eased, while Brent (+0.474%) caught a late bid on Putin escalation headlines.

themes.evidence: Core PCE inline but USD own impulse +0.107%; USD/CHF +30.8 pips, USD/CAD +39.2 pips, EUR/USD -21.7 pips.
Australia CPI beat at 03:30: AUD +0.167% own impulse; AUD/NZD +84.2 pips daily, AUD/USD +13.5 pips while NZD/USD -30.1 pips; NZD weakest overall -0.352%.

themes.theme: Geopolitical risk premium in oil, not FX vol
themes.evidence: Brent +0.474%, USD/CAD +39.2 pips, late headline Putin said to plan Ukraine escalation; VIX -0.302, SPX -0.141.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped in three small up legs and three down legs; the only clear catalyst was the 14:30 US data leg down -23.0 pips, closing at 1.16497, -21.7 pips on the day.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: USD/JPY traded a 56.2-pip range with a final 45.0-pip up leg after the 14:30 US data, closing at 159.416 (+14.5 pips).
leg_notes.GBP/USD: After a small early 17.5-pip up leg, GBP/USD spent the rest of the day in a -62.2 pip down leg with no single catalyst, closing near its lows at 1.35903 (-44.4 pips).
leg_notes.USD/CHF: USD/CHF turned from a -18.0 pip early dip to a 47.4 pip up leg, closing +30.8 pips at 0.80558; the US data contributed +9.7 pips within that leg.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: AUD/USD ran up 33.3 pips early helped by Australia CPI, then gave back -18.4 pips after the US data, still closing +13.5 pips at 0.71687.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: USD/CAD had no clear drivers in its up 64.4 pip leg; it closed +39.2 pips at 1.38776 with the late geopolitical headline too weak to own the final dip.
leg_notes.NZD/USD: NZD/USD faded from an early +12.9 pips to a -41.4 pip down leg, closing -30.1 pips at 0.5939, with AUD CPI and US data only partial drivers.
leg_notes.EUR/CHF: EUR/CHF reversed a -16.1 pip dip into a +34.0 pip rally, closing +18.5 pips at 0.93847 with no clear single driver.
leg_notes.CHF/JPY: CHF/JPY fell in a -82.1 pip leg after an early +24.0 pip bounce, closing -58.1 pips at 197.879; AUD CPI was a partial driver at -14.7 pips.
leg_notes.AUD/NZD: AUD/NZD reversed from -19.1 pips to a +101.9 pip rally, closing +84.2 pips at 1.207; Australia CPI contributed +33.4 pips.
leg_notes.EUR/GBP: EUR/GBP recovered from -9.1 pips to +22.4 pips, closing +12.1 pips at 0.85719; US data contributed only +3.4 pips.
leg_notes.AUD/CHF: AUD/CHF turned from -8.3 pips to +41.5 pips, closing +33.2 pips at 0.5775; Australia CPI contributed +10.1 pips.
leg_notes.NZD/CHF: NZD/CHF whipsawed in small legs and ended -5.8 pips at 0.47842 with no clear catalyst.
leg_notes.USD/ZAR: USD/ZAR had a volatile 927.7-pip range; the final 835.4-pip up leg on US data and Putin headlines dominated, closing +403.5 pips at 15.9846.
leg_notes.USD/MXN: USD/MXN chopped in several legs with no single driver, closing +202.7 pips at 16.965 after a late 417.1-pip up leg.
leg_notes.Gold/USD: Gold fell in a -754.2 pip late leg to close -517.7 pips at 4590.77; the US data was noted but considered too weak to own the move.
leg_notes.BTC/USD: BTC/USD ended in a -1234.1 pip down leg, closing -1166.1 pips at 77987.2; US data contributed -414.3 pips of the leg.
leg_notes.Brent/USD: Brent recovered from a -310.5 pip decline into a +355.2 pip late up leg, closing +42.6 pips at 90.234 on the Putin escalation headline.

polarity_reads.read: AUD beat produced a normal 0.167% AUD impulse; the strongest response in AUD/NZD (+34.1 pips) and AUD/USD (+13.0 pips) shows the market was positioned for AUD upside and used the beat to extend long AUD/antipodean trades.

polarity_reads.event: Core PCE Price Index m/m +2 more
polarity_reads.read: An inline 0.2% core PCE still produced a 0.107% USD impulse with USD/CHF +9.3 pips and USD/JPY +12.3 pips, implying the market was short USD or read the data as not blocking further USD strength.

scenarios.name: USD strength persists, AUD outperforms
scenarios.thesis: The measured tape shows USD demand despite inline data and AUD demand on CPI; with Jackson Hole upcoming, the market continues to favor USD and AUD against EUR, CHF, NZD.
triggers: USD Unemployment Claims prints at or below 208K forecast
Jackson Hole speakers reinforce higher-for-longer Fed
Putin headlines do not escalate further
scenarios.invalidation: A sharp risk-off or clearly dovish Jackson Hole breaks the USD bid.

pair_paths.rationale: Closed at lower end of 37.4-pip range, USD strength points lower.
Closed near highs of range, USD data bid supported.
AUD CPI beat still dominating, closed +13.5 pips.
NZD weakest; closed at low end of range.
Gold already -517.7 pips; USD strength pressures.

scenarios.name: Geopolitical escalation / risk-off
scenarios.thesis: Putin escalation headline gains traction; oil and safe haven JPY outperform, while growth-sensitive AUD and NZD fade.
scenarios.invalidation: De-escalation news or strong risk-on equity rally.

pair_paths.rationale: JPY safe-haven demand dominates risk-off, reversing USD/JPY from highs.
Risk-off bid for gold after a -517.7 pip selloff.
Oil risk premium rises on escalation; Brent already +42.6 pips on the headline.
High-beta AUD fades as risk appetite worsens.
NZD remains weakest and vulnerable in risk-off.

scenarios.name: Risk-on / dovish Jackson Hole reversal
scenarios.thesis: If Jackson Hole signals lower rates and geopolitical fears ease, the overbought USD and commodity underperformance reverse; AUD and NZD lead, gold/BTC bounce.
scenarios.invalidation: Strong US data or fresh escalation keeps USD bid.

pair_paths.rationale: Dovish Fed repricing weakens USD; EUR/USD rebounds from lower end of range.
GBP/USD was oversold after -44.4 pips, room to retrace range.
AUD strength extends as risk appetite recovers.
NZD shorts unwind from a -30.1 pip close near lows.
Risk-on rebound in crypto after -1166.1 pip decline.

risks.risk: Putin escalation headlines after the close
risks.why_it_matters: Brent +0.474% and USD/CAD +39.2 pips already reflect geopolitical premium; further escalation could reverse risk appetite and pressure AUD/NZD.
USD strength after inline PCE suggests market is positioned for hawkish Fed; any dovish signal could produce sharp USD downside, especially EUR/USD near low end of 37.4 range.
Medium impact data at 14:30 can validate or dent the USD bid; prior 206K, forecast 208K.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: 14:30 US Unemployment Claims (forecast 208K, previous 206K) and 18:15 Jackson Hole Symposium are the key events; they can either extend the USD bid or trigger a dovish reversal, with AUD/NZD and gold/BTC most sensitive to any risk shift.
